text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx spike on streaming-gateway across multiple regions. Alert threshold exceeded (5m). Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/streaming-5xx

sam: oncall here, looking now. any initial customer impact notes?

maya: quick check: logs show a mix of upstream 502/504 from model-proxy and a lot of 'chunked encoding: unexpected EOF' on gateway workers. also saw surge in client cancellations around the same time. past 10m: 12% 5xx on streaming endpoints, non-streamed endpoints ~1%.

ryan: seeing queue_length spike on gateway LB and CONNECT resets from idle clients. possible connection backlog causing worker thrash. env shows gateway replica CPU healthy but accept queue growing.

lee: copying some log snippets:
```
2026-03-14T07:08:12Z gateway-1 write tcp 10.10.3.12:443->10.20.1.45:51832: write: connection reset by peer
2026-03-14T07:08:14Z gateway-1 stream_handler.go:278 chunked-encode: unexpected EOF while flushing
2026-03-14T07:09:02Z model-proxy-3 upstream 502 Bad Gateway: downstream closed connection
```

maya: repro with curl-ish (non-prod):
```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \ 
  "https://gateway.prod.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-large" 
# clients see mid-stream close with no trailer
```

tess: are we sure this is gateway vs model-proxy? which side is failing first?

maya: timeline: gateway started responding with 502s at 07:07Z, model-proxy logs show increased latency and occasional OOM-ish restart traces a minute later. hypothesis: a small set of clients are hammering long-lived streaming sessions causing KV cache pressure -> proxy latency -> backpressure to gateway -> connections time out/close. also saw a burst of large prompt sizes from a few API keys.

sam: immediate mitigations we can attempt (short term):
- enable streaming->paged fallback for non-critical tiers (feature flag)
- apply temporary rate-limit on open-streams per API key (200 -> 50)
- scale gateway replicas by +2 in critical regions, and add upstream model-proxy pod capacity
- route 10% of traffic to standby region (ramp) to shed load

ryan: I'll open a quick k8s scale: `kubectl scale deployment/gateway --replicas=7 -n prod` and `kubectl scale deployment/model-proxy --replicas=6 -n prod` now. watch logs and latency.

alexa: enabling fallback flag for customer-tier=free and tier=dev now: `POST /admin/flags/fallback?env=prod&percent=100&target=free` -> response 200.

support-bot: customer impact summary (so far):
- customer-acme: intermittent stream disconnects since 07:06Z, retries succeed ~60%
- customer-nova: page errors on long sessions >2min
- ~2200 unique API keys hit an error in 10m window, top 5 keys make up 40% of streaming connections

sam: good. alexa + ryan + maya coordinate on rollout. maya can you tail the chunking errors and post a sample after mitigation?

maya: on it. tailing logs. applied a quick patch to gateway config to increase read timeout from 30s -> 60s to reduce spurious close (will monitor for head-of-line effects).

lee: also flipped an experimental fix in staging yesterday that drops invalid chunk frames more gracefully. could be useful if we backport a hotfix. but that requires a gateway restart for prod.

ryan: scaling applied, flags enabled. early metrics: 1m post-mitigation 5xx down to 6.5% from 12%. connection resets dropping. still seeing some EOF chunked errs though.

tess: any customer-facing comms planned? DS/CS?

sam: yes, brief comms — internal status + ETA. tagging CS to draft. @support-bot pull affected customer list for outreach.

support-bot: outreach list queued. will send templated note to top-10 impacted customers with links to workarounds (switch to paged, reduce prompt size, increase client keepalive).

alexa: note: we observed a single API key (key_ABC123) creating 40% of long-lived streams with huge prompt sizes; we've throttled that key as part of rate-limit gating.

maya: extracted a focused stack trace that shows the chunk serializer aborting on partial frames. adding the snippet to thread:
```
stream_serializer.go:142 flush failed: unexpected EOF while writing chunk header
stack: github.com/redwood/stream.(*Serializer).Flush
	/internal/stream/serializer.go:142
```

ryan: live checklist for oncall (do this now):
- [x] scale gateway + model-proxy
- [x] enable streaming->paged fallback for dev/free
- [x] throttle top offending API keys (temporary)
- [ ] deploy graceful-chunk-drop hotfix (requires restart) (maya/lee)
- [ ] roll traffic to standby region 10% -> 50% (gradual) (sam/ryan)

sam: handing off at 07:31Z to maya for sustained mitigation and hotfix deploy. I'll summarize and file a postmortem once stabilized. next oncall pls pick up 08:00Z if not resolved.

maya: taking over. current status summary for handoff: 5xx rate reduced from 12% -> 6.5%, primary mitigation (fallback + throttles + scale) applied. hotfix candidate ready, target deploy in 10m with a canary on one gateway pod. impact: partial for long-stream customers, many can use paged as workaround.

lee: prepping the restart plan: canary restart gateway-1 in az-a first, watch 1m metrics (5xx, conn reset). rollback via kubectl rollout undo if metrics worsen.

alexa: recording steps for post-incident notes: timeline, root causes (client long-lived surge + chunk parser fragility + backlog), mitigations, customers impacted, follow-ups (rate-limit rules, streaming quota dashboard, graceful-chunk-drop hotfix, runbook update).

support-bot: ETA for customer comms draft 08:00Z.

maya: canary deployed. monitoring... canary shows chunked EOFs reduced by ~80% on that pod. no user visible regressions so far.

sam: thanks everyone. I'll close the pager if we stay stable for 30m. handoff notes appended to oncall log. please add any follow-ups to the incident board.

ryan: follow-ups I own: postmortem queries, alert tuning (differentiate client-cancel vs gateway-5xx), and autoscale policy to pre-scale on streaming surge signals.

lee: I'll work with runtime team to get graceful-chunk-drop into the next patch release and plan a Q/A run to ensure no regression.

alexa: adding a tracking ticket: INF-5132 "Streaming chunked EOFs under load" and linking this thread.

maya: final note before handoff: recommend adding a metric for 'active long-lived streams per API key' to alert when top keys exceed threshold. saved search: `sum(active_streams) by api_key`

sam: signing off from active triage, leaving monitoring and hotfix to maya/lee. will re-open if it regresses. :white_check_mark:
